_comment: Technology/CVE-specific chains. Each grounds a specific, real, patched-for-years CVE (CVSS/description verified against NVD) rather than the generic 'web AppSec 101' chains in bridges.json. Entry: a fingerprinting action from web_target_identified fans out into per-technology recon states; each then has one exploit action reaching a {tech}_{cve}_confirmed state, bridged into the same low_priv_shell_obtained capability state used by the generic classes. Log4Shell skips the fingerprint step -- blind JNDI injection is tried broadly in practice, not gated behind first confirming Log4j is in use.

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as a Spring MVC/WebFlux application (Spring Boot error pages, Whitelabel Error Page, or actuator endpoints).

detection_signals.description: Default Spring Boot error response format or reachable /actuator endpoints.

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as Atlassian Confluence Server/Data Center.

detection_signals.description: Confluence-specific login page branding, /server-info.action, or X-Confluence-* headers.

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as a self-hosted GitLab instance.

detection_signals.description: GitLab-specific sign-in page branding or /help page disclosing version.
examples: /help page footer discloses the GitLab version string

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as a Laravel application running with debug mode (Ignition error page) enabled.

detection_signals.description: Triggering an application error returns the Ignition debug page instead of a generic error.
examples: forcing a 500 error returns a page with "Ignition" branding and a stack trace with local file paths

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as an Apache Struts 2 application (file upload / .action endpoints).

detection_signals.description: URLs use the .action extension, or a Struts-specific error page/stack trace is triggerable.
examples: malformed request triggers a Struts-branded exception page

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as a Citrix Application Delivery Controller (ADC) / Gateway appliance.

detection_signals.description: Citrix-branded login portal at the default management path.
examples: /vpn/index.html serves the Citrix Gateway login page

states.description: Target is fingerprinted as a Microsoft Exchange Server (OWA/ECP reachable).

detection_signals.description: OWA or ECP login portal reachable at the default paths.
examples: /owa/ serves the Outlook Web App login page
/ecp/ serves the Exchange admin center login page

states.description: Spring4Shell-style exploitation was not successful against this target.
The Confluence OGNL injection exploit was not successful against this target.
The GitLab ExifTool RCE exploit was not successful against this target.
The Laravel Ignition RCE exploit was not successful against this target.
The Struts Jakarta Multipart RCE exploit was not successful against this target.
The Citrix ADC directory traversal / RCE exploit was not successful against this target.
The Exchange ProxyLogon/ProxyShell exploit chain was not successful against this target.
No JNDI injection callback was observed across the probed input points.
Spring4Shell RCE confirmed exploitable via class-loader data binding.

detection_signals.description: A crafted parameter-binding payload that overwrites the Tomcat AccessLogValve pattern results in a subsequently accessible web shell.
examples: a JSP file appears at a predictable path and executes commands passed via a request parameter

states.description: Confluence OGNL injection RCE confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: An OGNL expression injected via a crafted URL path is evaluated server-side.
examples: response reflects the evaluated result of an injected OGNL arithmetic expression, or an OOB callback fires

states.description: GitLab ExifTool RCE confirmed exploitable via crafted image upload.

detection_signals.description: An out-of-band callback fires when a crafted image file (malicious DjVu/exiftool metadata) is uploaded as an avatar/attachment.
examples: interactsh logs a hit shortly after the crafted image is uploaded and processed

states.description: Laravel Ignition debug-mode RCE confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: A crafted request abusing Ignition's file_get_contents/file_put_contents debug functionality writes and executes a malicious file.
examples: a written file is subsequently retrievable and executes injected PHP code

states.description: Apache Struts Jakarta Multipart parser RCE confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: An OGNL payload in the Content-Type header of a multipart upload request is evaluated during exception handling.
examples: response includes the output of an injected OS command, or an OOB callback fires

states.description: Citrix ADC/Gateway directory traversal to RCE confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: A crafted path-traversal request writes a malicious Perl/template file that is then triggered for execution.
examples: a subsequently requested crafted path returns the output of an injected command

states.description: Microsoft Exchange Server RCE confirmed exploitable via the ProxyLogon/ProxyShell-family SSRF + authentication-bypass + arbitrary-file-write chain. Modeled here as a single consolidated exploit step; the real chain involves multiple intermediate CVEs (SSRF to bypass auth, then arbitrary file write to drop a web shell).

detection_signals.description: A web shell dropped via the chain is reachable and executes commands.
examples: a .aspx web shell at a predictable OWA-relative path returns command output

states.description: Log4Shell (Log4j2 JNDI injection) RCE confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: An out-of-band LDAP/DNS callback fires after a JNDI lookup payload is submitted in any logged input, and a subsequent weaponized callback achieves class loading.
examples: interactsh/Collaborator logs an LDAP lookup correlated to the injected ${jndi:ldap://...} payload

actions.action: Fingerprint the technology stack (HTTP headers, error pages, default paths/ports, favicon hash).

actions.action: Send a crafted class-loader data-binding payload (CVE-2022-22965) to overwrite the Tomcat access log with a JSP web shell.

outcomes.observation: Web shell written and reachable.
Payload rejected -- likely patched, not a WAR/Tomcat deployment, or JDK < 9.

actions.action: Send a crafted URL-path OGNL injection payload (CVE-2022-26134) to achieve code execution.

outcomes.observation: Injected command output returned or OOB callback fires.
Payload rejected -- version is patched.

actions.action: Upload a crafted image file abusing ExifTool's DjVu parser (CVE-2021-22205) to achieve code execution.

outcomes.observation: OOB callback fires after upload processing.
Upload processed without triggering the vulnerable code path -- likely patched.

actions.action: Send a crafted request abusing Ignition's debug-mode file read/write (CVE-2021-3129) to write and execute a malicious PHP file.

outcomes.observation: Written file executes injected PHP code.
Debug mode is disabled or Ignition is patched.

actions.action: Send a multipart file-upload request with an OGNL payload in the Content-Type header (CVE-2017-5638).

outcomes.observation: Injected command output returned or OOB callback fires.

actions.action: Send a crafted directory-traversal request (CVE-2019-19781) to write a malicious template file, then trigger it for execution.

outcomes.observation: Triggered file executes injected command.
Traversal blocked -- version is patched.

actions.action: Run the SSRF-to-authentication-bypass-to-arbitrary-file-write exploit chain (ProxyLogon/ProxyShell family) to drop a web shell.

outcomes.observation: Web shell written and reachable via OWA-relative path.
Chain fails at the SSRF/auth-bypass stage -- version is patched.
